findings.title: Reject corrupted blob deduplication hits before acknowledging new revisions
findings.description: INSERT OR IGNORE trusts an existing tenant/digest row without validating its bytes. A fresh request supplying valid bytes can receive a durable success receipt and new head pointing to corrupt bytes already in storage. The new revision cannot be read immediately after successful acceptance.
repro: Submit module a, object x=b'original', base=None.
Using an owned SQLite connection, UPDATE native_blobs SET content=b'corrupt'; close the connection.
Submit a new module b, object x=b'original', base=None, using a fresh request key.
Observe received and committed b head; read(org,b,new_revision,x) raises Object integrity failure.
findings.expected: Detect and reject the corrupted existing content inside the transaction, rolling back new revisions/heads/receipts, or perform an explicitly validated recovery policy.
findings.scope: Requires preexisting storage corruption; no authentication bypass or ordinary healthy-store lost update was demonstrated.

review_coverage: Read all frozen store/CLI/test source and design.

Checked structural field/type/path validation, tenant/module revision predicates, stable-key request normalization, transactional rollback, base/read/write conflict checks, exact dependency traversal and contradictory pins.
Independently ran tests forbidding process/network use in core calls, and actual CLI processes from a temporary directory without Git metadata.
coverage_limits: Trusted host authentication and authorization are outside these APIs; tenant/actor strings are not evidence of authentication.
Caller declarations do not establish complete read sets; no proof of host read capture was supplied.
Conflict checks compare current versus base content digests, not per-object mutation history; no guarantee against arbitrary ABA history is asserted.
Thread suite submits 250 jobs with 16 worker threads; process script uses at most 16 simultaneous CLI processes. Neither proves 250 simultaneously running workers.
No forced process termination, power-loss durability, disk exhaustion, multi-host replicas, network filesystem, Linux execution, production capacity, or token savings independently validated.
Composition validates revision/dependency metadata, not all blob bytes or business approval.
Review is limited to frozen source and supplemental process verification script; no claim of defect absence beyond exercised cases.

cleanup.notes: Initial repro cleanup hit a retained sqlite handle; process exited and exact owned files were removed after path validation. A generic PowerShell recursive cleanup was blocked by tool policy; explicit validated file unlink cleanup succeeded. Default python WindowsApps alias was unusable; explicit runtime resolved testing.
